method: analyzer key tree (tree-sitter-yaml 0.7.1, concrete syntax, YAML 1.2 core schema) compared against an INDEPENDENT document-model oracle (PyYAML 6.0.1 compose, YAML 1.1). Only the key tree is compared, because that is the most both implementations can independently see; scalar type resolution differs BY DESIGN between a 1.1 and a 1.2 schema and is a known fact about YAML rather than a defect in either. Merge keys are not applied on either side (PyYAML's flatten_mapping runs in the constructor, which compose never reaches). Every disagreement is adjudicated into one of nine declared buckets; anything not explained by a bucket is reported as a defect.
samplingRule: deterministic stride over each corpus's sorted file list, stride = floor(files/draw), so a head-slice's alphabetical bias cannot pick one subtree; 200 files per corpus

coverageByGrammarHealth.note: tree-sitter-yaml 0.7.1 cannot lex a MULTI-LINE DOUBLE-QUOTED SCALAR (a `description:` broken across a line break). CORRECTED 2026-09-28 by script/m60/yaml-bucket-audit.ts: an earlier version of this note said the trigger produces a 58-byte ERROR at the document root. The 58-byte node is real but NESTED (v1.28: bytes 79,218-79,276, line 2453, depth 4). The ROOT node itself is the ERROR, and it is large: measured over docker/api/docs/v1.25..v1.38 the root ERROR spans 72,809-110,341 bytes and the resulting tree covers only 27.6-31.1% of the file, so 69-72% of each file is NEVER PARSED. That is the actual mechanism of the loss — the parser stops, rather than one token eating containment — and it is why the analyzer publishes 1,991-2,637 key-tree paths where PyYAML finds 7,249-9,001. A path-level audit (yaml-bucket-audit.ts) attributes 88,675 lost paths across the 15 files with 0 that the grammar does not explain. Measured trigger: docker/api/docs/v1.25.yaml .. v1.38.yaml plus one Cloud Build file, all of which PyYAML parses cleanly. Filed against the GRAMMAR under the M60 fork policy and NOT charged to the analyzer; what the analyzer does about the damage it does receive is measured above.
